# Results — Study 309 (OJ-Frost) on the real OJ=F tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The freeze trade — buy
frozen-concentrate OJ futures (`OJ=F`) in the window after a hard Florida freeze — and the
Dec–Feb winter-seasonality variant, run on the Yahoo! continuous front-month OJ future.
Freeze dates come from the hardcoded table in [`oj_frost/data.py`](../oj_frost/data.py).
Reactive entry uses one documented execution lag (enter the first session **after** the
freeze, never the freeze-day move). As-of **2026-05-31** (the partial June 2026 month is
dropped); match the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | Days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| OJ=F | 2001-09-17 → 2026-05-29 | 6,198 | `1b3126f827b9` |

The single most important number on this page: **the Yahoo OJ=F tape begins in
September 2001.** Of the 12 severe Florida freezes in the hardcoded table, **8 predate the
tape entirely** — including every freeze from the 1977–1989 cluster that the *Trading
Places* lore (and the film itself) is built on. Only **4 freezes** are tradable on this
tape: Jan 2003, Jan 2009, Jan 2010, Jan 2022.

## The freeze event study — reactive entry (lag = 1), gross

| Forward window | n | win-rate | mean (bps) | HAC *t* | placebo pct | excess vs random |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 sessions  | 4 | **0%**  | **−240** | −4.51 | 17% | −243 |
| 10 sessions | 4 | 25% | −340 | −1.85 | 17% | −353 |
| 21 sessions | 4 | 25% | −392 | −1.54 | 20% | −420 |

Per-event 5-session returns (bps): **−338, −326, −44, −250** — every one **negative**. The
*Trading Places* trade is supposed to make money when a freeze hits; on the only four
freezes in the modern tradable tape, OJ futures **fell** over the following week, every
time.

> **Read the −4.51 honestly.** With **n = 4** identically-signed events the HAC *t* and the
> block-bootstrap CI are degenerate — that statistic is not evidence of a robust *negative*
> edge, it is evidence that **there is no usable sample**. Four events cannot certify a
> signal in either direction. The honest reading is **no signal**, with a wink that what
> little data exists points the *wrong* way for the folklore.

## The un-tradable ceiling — perfect foresight (lag = 0)

Even if you could enter on the freeze session's close (you can't — you don't know the crop
damage yet), the 5-session window still averages **−360 bps** (*t* = −3.83). The freeze-day
reaction is not a pop you missed by being slow; on this tape it simply isn't there.

## Winter seasonality (Dec–Feb vs rest of year), daily, gross

| Bucket | n (days) | mean (bps/day) |
|---|--:|--:|
| Winter (DJF) | 1,505 | −6.2 |
| Rest of year | 4,692 | +3.5 |
| **Difference** | — | **−9.7** (HAC *t* = **−1.36**) |

The "cold risk is priced into OJ in winter" story also fails: winter days are if anything
slightly *worse* than the rest of the year, and the difference is statistically
indistinguishable from zero (|t| < 2).

## Positive control — the engine works

On the deterministic synthetic tape with a planted post-freeze spike (`freeze_jump = 0.20`,
front-loaded over a 5-session window) the same event study recovers the effect at HAC
*t* > 2 and a placebo percentile > 0.95; with the jump set to zero it is quiet (|t| < 2).
The pipeline can bank a planted freeze edge — it finds none on the real tape because none
is there.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Only 4 freezes are in the tradable OJ=F tape, and all 4 saw OJ *fall*
  over the next week. n = 4 cannot certify anything; the apparent −4.51 *t* is a degenerate
  small-sample artefact, not a real (negative) edge. Winter seasonality is insignificant
  (*t* = −1.36). There is no statistically real freeze signal here.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Nothing to trade: the famous freezes predate the tape, the
  in-tape freezes go the wrong way, and OJ=F is a thin, wide-spread contract where even a
  real edge would be eaten by costs. A folklore trade with no modern data behind it.
- **The *Trading Places* trade? — BUSTED.** The movie's premise (corner the OJ market ahead
  of a frost report) is great cinema and, on every freeze we can actually measure, a
  money-loser. The lore lives entirely in freezes that happened before anyone could pull a
  daily OJ=F bar off Yahoo.
